- **Representation of All Classes**: It guarantees that the test data accurately represents all classes in the dataset, preventing scenarios where the test set might be dominated by one class and fail to evaluate the model’s performance on minority classes effectively.

- **Avoiding Skewed Evaluations**: Without stratification, the test set might accidentally end up with an overrepresentation or underrepresentation of certain classes, leading to misleading performance metrics for the machine learning model.

- **Better Model Generalization**: By maintaining the class distribution, the model is trained and tested on data that reflects real-world scenarios, improving its ability to generalize and perform well on unseen data.

- **Removes Redundant Majority Class Samples**: Tomek Links identifies and eliminates samples from the majority class that are **near or overlapping with minority class samples**. This is done by pairing samples from different classes that are nearest neighbors to each other. If a sample from the majority class is paired with a minority class sample, it is removed from the majority class. This reduces redundancy and prevents the model from being biased toward the majority class.

This approach ensures that the machine learning model has a better chance of accurately detecting the minority class (e.g., anemic patients) without being skewed by the majority class.
